prompt: High-fidelity product UI concept image for a native macOS 14 app named Ledge. Horizontal 16:10 presentation, 1600x1000 feel, no device mockup, no marketing poster. Show TWO coherent native app surfaces side by side on a deep near-black field: left, the real Ledge notch panel physically growing downward from a centered MacBook notch at the top edge, width about 740 px, with a thin calibrated module rail around the notch, an elegant Media module open with album artwork, track title, restrained transport controls and one refined violet progress wavelength; right, the Ledge Settings window with a macOS sidebar and an Appearance detail page using the exact same visual system. Art direction: precision optical bench and spectrograph, black smoked glass, graphite, satin anodized aluminum, bone-white typography, electric violet and very restrained mint spectral hairlines only for live state. One continuous surface, hairline seams instead of floating cards, strong hierarchy, ample quiet negative space, SF Pro-like typography, tiny monospaced measurements only as secondary annotation. The notch is the unmistakable aperture and anchor. Settings sidebar entries are in French and readable: Général, Apparence, Modules, Profils, Affichage, Permissions, Raccourcis, À propos. Appearance view shows a large live notch preview and a few precisely aligned controls, not a dense form. Premium Apple-native, calm, obvious to any user, accessible contrast, no gradients, no glowing neon, no glassmorphism blobs, no nested cards, no fake browser chrome, no illegible gibberish, no excessive sci-fi HUD. This is a visual direction comp, polished enough to guide SwiftUI implementation.
